newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle trade brisk at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Tuesday sold at $72.00 per cwt in brisk activity, steady with last week, feedlot sources said.

About 40,000 head traded in Kansas, which brought the week to date figure to 53,200, USDA and private sources said. An estimated 30,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. which brought the weeklly figure to about 37,000, they said.
Cattle prices were underpinned by tight supplies of finished cattle, with some feedyards selling cattle originally scheduled for sale in December, the feedlot sources said.
Firm packer demand was fueled by continued moderate beef sales, market sources said.
Retailers reportedly were booking orders for beef promotions, which seasonally run between Thanksgiving and Christmas, the sources said.
Beef prices were quoted up $1.46 to $1.69 per cwt for choice cuts and up $0.12 to down $0.42 for selects, according to USDA. There were 253 fabricated beef loads sold.
